open_points.subject: A3 INV-009 duplicate-active refusal contract
open_points.text: a pair with an active record is refused and nothing changes
open_points.question: What failure may callers rely on when an active assignment or grant already exists?
options: A common typed duplicate-active failure for all three operations
A generic conflict failure shared with other access-management conflicts
open_points.default_guess: A common typed duplicate-active failure for all three operations
consequences: Callers can handle reassignment and both grant duplicates uniformly
Callers cannot distinguish an active duplicate from other conflicts
open_points.requirement: a pair with an active record is refused and nothing changes

witness.initial: An active record already exists for one staff, viewer, or service-principal project pair.
events: An administrator invokes the corresponding assignment or grant operation again.
outcomes: The caller receives a recognizable duplicate-active failure.
The caller receives an undifferentiated conflict failure.

open_points.subject: A3 INV-009 concurrent creation
open_points.text: and the storage refuses a second active record for a pair inserted past that check.
open_points.question: When concurrent requests both pass the active-record check and the storage rejects one, must the losing operation return the same duplicate-active refusal as an ordinary duplicate, or may it return a storage/internal failure?
options: Return the ordinary duplicate-active refusal and change nothing
Return a distinct concurrency conflict and change nothing
Expose a storage/internal failure while preserving the invariant
open_points.default_guess: Return the ordinary duplicate-active refusal and change nothing

witness.initial: A pair has revoked history but no active record.
events: Administrator A and administrator B concurrently request a new active record for the same pair.
Both requests pass the operation-level active-record check.
The storage accepts one insertion and rejects the other.
outcomes: One request succeeds and the loser receives the ordinary duplicate-active refusal.
One request succeeds and the loser receives a storage/internal error.
witness.observer: The administrator or API client that made the losing request

open_points.subject: A3 INV-009 storage coverage
open_points.text: and the storage refuses a second active record for a pair inserted past that check.
open_points.question: Must the Required tests demonstrate storage-level rejection independently for staff assignments, viewer grants, and producer grants, or is one representative storage check sufficient?
options: Demonstrate the storage guarantee for all three record kinds
Demonstrate only the viewer and producer grant stores
open_points.default_guess: Demonstrate the storage guarantee for all three record kinds

witness.initial: Each of the three record kinds already has an active record for a pair.
events: A Factory check attempts to insert a second active staff assignment directly.
It repeats the attempt for a viewer grant and a producer grant.
outcomes: All three rejected insertions are asserted.
Only one record kind is checked, leaving the other storage implementations unconstrained.
witness.observer: The Factory verification gate and a later implementer

open_points.subject: A3 INV-009 repeated revoke/regrant history
open_points.text: a pair whose only record is revoked receives a new active record and the revoked one is unchanged
open_points.question: What must the Required tests show when a pair has multiple revoked historical records after repeated revoke-and-regrant cycles and no active record?
options: A further new active record is created and every revoked record remains unchanged
Only the first regrant after one revoked record must be tested
Repeated regrant history is not supported
open_points.default_guess: A further new active record is created and every revoked record remains unchanged

witness.initial: A pair has two revoked historical records and no active record after two completed grant-and-revoke cycles.
events: An administrator grants or assigns the pair again.
outcomes: A third, new active record is created and both revoked records remain unchanged.
The operation refuses the request or fails because the implementation only supports one revoked predecessor.
witness.observer: The administrator and the audit-history reader

open_points.subject: A3 INV-009 storage refusal effects
open_points.text: and the storage refuses a second active record for a pair inserted past that check.
open_points.question: Must the storage-level Required test also assert that the rejected insertion leaves the existing active record, all revoked history, and all other state unchanged?
options: Assert the entire relevant storage state is unchanged
Assert only that no second active record exists
Assert only that the insert reports a failure
open_points.default_guess: Assert the entire relevant storage state is unchanged

open_points.subject: A31 concurrency security review
open_points.text: - concurrency: APPLICABLE; references: A8, A18, A19, A22, A29; affected: replay identities, single active budget version, bootstrap
open_points.question: After INV-009 moved from A8 to A3 and gained storage-enforced uniqueness for three access-record kinds, must the concurrency category reference A3 and name concurrent assignment/grant creation as affected, or is INV-009 intentionally outside this security-review category?
options: Add A3 and concurrent assignment/grant creation
Declare explicitly why INV-009 is outside the concurrency category
Leave the existing references and affected list unchanged
open_points.default_guess: Add A3 and concurrent assignment/grant creation
